newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl and mining union meet to tackle coal crisis.
newsitem.headline: Kohl and mining union meet to tackle coal crisis.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl and mining union leader Hans Berger began a meeting on Thursday aimed at reaching a compromise over a government plan to cut subsidies which has enraged Germany's 90,000 miners.
Kohl and Berger met in Kohl's chancellery amid reports that Kohl was prepared to offer more government money to cushion the effect of the cuts which miners say will cost 50,000 jobs.

As the two sides met, tens of thousands of miners were standing by in nearby Cologne and the Ruhr valley coal-and-steel heartland, ready to resume their protests in Bonn if the outcome of the talks did not satisfy them.

The miners had virtually besieged Bonn's government quarter for three days, but withdrew on Wednesday after Kohl cancelled talks planned for Tuesday at short notice saying he would not negotiate in a climate of intimidation.
Bonn plans to cut the level of annual subsidies to 3.8 billion marks ($2.2 billion) by 2005 from over nine billion marks at present.

The mass-circulation daily newspaper Bild said Kohl was ready to offer an extra 300 million marks a year for the next three years to delay some pit closures, as long as the Social Democrat-led government of the mining state of North Rhine-Westphalia increasd its own subsidies over the next eight years.
Berger was due to hold a news conference on the results of the talks at noon (1100 GMT). ($ = 1.695 German Marks)
